input.answer: I'd go with option 1, the one with the company first in each row. The S&P 500 group is right at the top with all 12 companies (מנורה, הראל, מגדל, הפניקס, כלל...) sorted cheapest fee first, so I could pick one in a minute. Fairly sure. Option 3 is the one they marked מומלץ, but it's a wall of percents in brown boxes and I gave up on it.

stuck.where: Top of screen 1, the three buttons 1/2/3
stuck.why: I didn't get at first that these were three versions of the same list. I thought they were tabs
It goes company by company. I had to thumb through all 16 of הראל's tracks and 15 of מור's to compare S&P funds, and got bored halfway through מור

Twelve columns of nearly the same 0.5–0.7% numbers in brown shades. I couldn't tell which colour was good, didn't read the small line above that explains it, and the S&P column sits at the far right next to the names, so the rest I barely looked at

stuck.where: מניות / מט"ח rows with little rings
stuck.why: Didn't know what the ring and the 99% mean for me, so I skipped them

findings.what: Every row repeats the same words: מניות, מט"ח, מההחסכון, מההפקדה, פחות מ־3 שנים, plus the clock icons. I re-read them each time just to find the one number that's different
The fees are only small percents (0.52% vs 0.71%). They look like nothing. No shekel amount, so I can't feel the difference
The grid's colour isn't explained right next to it. I guessed darker means cheaper but I'm not sure
Grouping by company makes comparing the same kind of fund across companies a very long scroll
The 'מומלץ' option is the hardest one to read on a phone, with 12 columns of percents
Lots of rows show 'פחות מ־3 שנים' instead of a return, which makes them look weaker or suspicious
איילון with only 34% and a half ring and 'עוד לא דווח' looked off, scary
Unexplained rings and coloured dots
